request: Analyze GSE324693 for PMID 41889117 (Systemic Consequences of Chronic Ethanol Intake: From Microbiome Shifts to Metabolic Impairment.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq, subcutaneous white adipose tissue (S2.4.16.p1)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of 60 weeks of 20% EtOH in drinking water vs water (control) on subcutaneous WAT gene expression in aged female C57BL/6 mice (S2.2.p1, S3.4.p3). There is no exercise intervention: the treadmill was used only as a time-to-fatigue performance test (S2.4.2.p1, week 55), given to every mouse in both groups.
final.inclusion: 17 female mice (7 control, 10 EtOH); RNA-seq on 6 vs 6 (GEO); paper figure n 5-6 control / 6-9 EtOH (FIG7)
planned_contrasts: EtOH vs Control in WAT (S3.4.p3; paper: 61 DEGs, 47 down / 14 up)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none (one WAT sample per mouse at sacrifice)
final.paper_method: Rsubread featureCounts; keep genes mapped in >= 6 samples; DESeq2 v1.44.0 (S2.4.16.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.2.p1: mice were randomized to 20% EtOH or water. S2.4.2.p1: treadmill endurance was an outcome test, not a training stimulus. S2.4.16.p1: WAT RNA-seq, DESeq2, FDR <= 0.1. S3.4.p3: 61 DEGs (47 down). The paper never compares exercised and non-exercised animals.

checks: GEO tissue = subcutaneous WAT, C57BL/6, Mus musculus, matching the paper
treatment Vehicle/EtOH, 6/6, matching the paper's two groups
data_processing: Rsubread + featureCounts raw counts, matching S2.4.16.p1

ownership.reasoning: The accession, tissue, strain, groups and processing all match the paper.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns S1.bam..S12.bam; the GEO titles are 'S1 ctrl'..'S12 EtOH'. The key is the S<n> token, an exact match on a named field, not position.

matrix.reasoning: Values are 100% integers, from 0 to 5.8e6; GEO data_processing says 'Raw counts matrix' from Rsubread/featureCounts. This matches the paper's DESeq2 input.

candidates.reason_rejected: EtOH vs water is an alcohol exposure, not exercise; reporting it as an exercise effect would change the estimand
every mouse took the same treadmill endurance test (S2.4.2.p1, FIG2 week 55); there is no unexercised comparison group and no exercise column in GEO

design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast: GSE324693 holds only Vehicle (water) vs EtOH WAT samples (6/6). Exercise appears in the paper only as a treadmill performance test given to all mice (S2.4.2.p1), so the data cannot identify an exercise effect on gene expression.
design.reasoning: The only grouping column is treatment (Vehicle 6 / EtOH 6). The task's estimand, an exercise effect, has no arm in the paper or the data.

discrepancies.paper: 17 mice (7 control/10 EtOH); FIG7 n 5-6 control / 6-9 EtOH
